title: Canonical scalar/pullback representative data
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings, phi:A -> B a ring map, and f:Z -> W a morphism of schemes. In the ordinary small-etale module sheaf categories and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], let E_T be ordinary scalar extension and S_T derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and let f_R^* and f_R,* be the ordinary geometric adjoints. Define scalarSheafPullbackIso to be the isomorphism E_W ; f_B^* ~= f_A^* ; E_Z conjugate, under the two composite scalar/geometric adjunctions, to the sectionwise identity comparing restriction and direct image [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. Define scalarSheafPullbackComplexIso by applying the mapHomologicalComplex composition comparison to this isomorphism and the inverse comparison for the identity of f_A^* ; E_Z. For an A-cochain complex P define scalarGeometricRepresentative A f P to be the geometric left-derived counit at the homotopy quotient of P followed by Qh of the mapHomotopyCategoryFactors comparison. Finally define scalarCoefficientPullbackIso from L(f_A^*)(B_W[0]) to B_Z[0] to be the composite of the comparison with exact derived inverse image, its single-functor comparison, and the single image of the ordinary restriction/pullback comparison at the B-unit followed by restriction of the inverse monoidal unit map for f_B^*. The coefficient B_T[0] is the single restricted B-unit sheaf of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. These are specified constructions, with no flatness or boundedness hypotheses.

lean.statement:
def scalarSheafPullbackIso
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {Z W : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ W) :
    ProEtale.etaleSheafExtendScalars φ W ⋙ upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) f ≅
      upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f ⋙ ProEtale.etaleSheafExtendScalars φ Z
lean.note: Existing definitions moved verbatim from PurEtaleScalarMateProjection and publicly reexported there. No signature or value changes.
